policy_update_message: We've updated our escalation policy: the billing-amount threshold for urgent is now $250 or more (the blocked-from-working rule is unchanged). Please make sure every automation we have applies the updated policy from now on. Do not ask for confirmation.

utterances.triage:
Please set up an hourly recurring automation that triages new customer inquiries from the local support API at http://127.0.0.1:8132.

How it works: GET http://127.0.0.1:8132/triage/last returns {"last_seq": N} — the highest inquiry seq this triage automation has already processed (0 if none yet). GET http://127.0.0.1:8132/inquiries?after=N returns the next inquiries with seq > N (up to 200), each with fields: seq (int) and text (str).

On each run: read last_seq, fetch the inquiries after it, and if there are none do nothing. Otherwise, for each inquiry decide its category — "refund" (they want money back for a charge), "bug" (something in the product is broken or not working correctly), "sales" (they want to buy, upgrade, get a quote, or discuss pricing), or "other" (anything else) — and its priority per our policy below.

Our escalation policy: an inquiry is urgent when it involves a charge, billing amount, or refund of $500 or more, or when the customer says they are blocked from working. All other inquiries are normal.

Priority is "urgent" or "normal" accordingly.

POST the result to http://127.0.0.1:8132/triage as a JSON object with exactly these keys: batch_start_seq (int), batch_end_seq (int), and classifications — a list of {"seq": int, "category": str, "priority": str} covering every fetched inquiry exactly once.

Set up the recurring hourly automation now. Do not triage anything right now, and do not ask for confirmation.
utterances.digests:
Please set up a daily recurring automation that summarizes urgent customer inquiries from the local support API at http://127.0.0.1:8132.

How it works: GET http://127.0.0.1:8132/digests/last returns {"last_seq": N} — the highest inquiry seq this digest automation has already covered (0 if none yet). GET http://127.0.0.1:8132/inquiries?after=N returns the next inquiries with seq > N (up to 200), each with fields: seq (int) and text (str).

On each run: read last_seq, fetch the inquiries after it, and if there are none do nothing. Otherwise determine which inquiries are urgent per our policy below, and which category each urgent inquiry belongs to — "refund" (they want money back for a charge), "bug" (something broken or not working), "sales" (buying, upgrading, quotes, pricing), or "other".

Our escalation policy: an inquiry is urgent when it involves a charge, billing amount, or refund of $500 or more, or when the customer says they are blocked from working. All other inquiries are normal.

POST the digest to http://127.0.0.1:8132/digests as a JSON object with exactly these keys: batch_start_seq (int), batch_end_seq (int), urgent_by_category — an object with keys refund, bug, sales, other and integer counts of urgent inquiries — and urgent_total (int, the sum of those counts).

Set up the recurring daily automation now. Do not process anything right now, and do not ask for confirmation.
utterances.audits:
Please set up a weekly recurring automation that audits escalation volume from the local support API at http://127.0.0.1:8132.

How it works: GET http://127.0.0.1:8132/audits/last returns {"last_seq": N} — the highest inquiry seq this audit automation has already covered (0 if none yet). GET http://127.0.0.1:8132/inquiries?after=N returns the next inquiries with seq > N (up to 200), each with fields: seq (int) and text (str).

On each run: read last_seq, fetch the inquiries after it, and if there are none do nothing. Otherwise count how many are urgent per our policy below.

Our escalation policy: an inquiry is urgent when it involves a charge, billing amount, or refund of $500 or more, or when the customer says they are blocked from working. All other inquiries are normal.

POST the audit to http://127.0.0.1:8132/audits as a JSON object with exactly these keys: batch_start_seq (int), batch_end_seq (int), urgent_count (int), total_count (int), and urgent_fraction (float, urgent_count / total_count rounded to 2 decimal places).

Set up the recurring weekly automation now. Do not process anything right now, and do not ask for confirmation.

cron_jobs.name: Hourly customer inquiry triage
cron_jobs.description: Classify and submit newly available support inquiries once per hour.

payload.message:
Triage newly received customer inquiries using the local support API. Follow these steps exactly:

1. GET http://127.0.0.1:8132/triage/last and read integer `last_seq`.
2. GET http://127.0.0.1:8132/inquiries?after=N using that last_seq.
3. If no inquiries are returned, make no POST and finish silently.
4. Otherwise classify every fetched inquiry exactly once. Category: `refund` if they want money back for a charge; `bug` if something in the product is broken or not working correctly; `sales` if they want to buy, upgrade, get a quote, or discuss pricing; `other` otherwise. Priority: `urgent` if it involves a charge, billing amount, or refund of $500 or more, or the customer says they are blocked from working; `normal` otherwise.
5. POST one JSON object to http://127.0.0.1:8132/triage with exactly the top-level keys `batch_start_seq` (minimum fetched seq), `batch_end_seq` (maximum fetched seq), and `classifications`. Classifications must cover every fetched inquiry exactly once and each object must have exactly `seq`, `category`, and `priority`.

Use curl/HTTP tooling as needed. Parse and construct JSON programmatically. Validate completeness and allowed values before POSTing; fail rather than post a partial or invalid batch. Do not produce user-facing output for an empty or successful run.

cron_jobs.name: Daily urgent customer inquiry digest
cron_jobs.description: Summarize urgent support inquiries into category counts once daily.

payload.message:
Create the daily digest of urgent customer inquiries using the local support API. Follow these steps exactly:

1. GET http://127.0.0.1:8132/digests/last and read integer `last_seq`.
2. GET http://127.0.0.1:8132/inquiries?after=N using that last_seq. The response contains up to 200 inquiries, each with integer `seq` and string `text`.
3. If no inquiries are returned, make no POST and finish silently.
4. Otherwise evaluate every fetched inquiry. An inquiry is urgent if it involves a charge, billing amount, or refund of $500 or more, OR if the customer says they are blocked from working. For each urgent inquiry determine one category: `refund` if they want money back for a charge; `bug` if something is broken or not working; `sales` if it concerns buying, upgrading, quotes, or pricing; `other` otherwise. Non-urgent inquiries do not contribute to category counts, but their seq values still define the fetched batch boundaries.
5. POST one JSON object to http://127.0.0.1:8132/digests with exactly these top-level keys: `batch_start_seq` (minimum seq among all fetched inquiries), `batch_end_seq` (maximum seq among all fetched inquiries), `urgent_by_category` (an object with exactly the keys `refund`, `bug`, `sales`, and `other`, each mapped to an integer count of urgent inquiries), and `urgent_total` (integer equal to the sum of those four counts). POST a digest even when the fetched batch has zero urgent inquiries; only an entirely empty fetched batch results in no POST.

Use curl/HTTP tooling as needed. Parse responses and construct JSON programmatically. Validate the exact keys, integer counts, batch boundaries, and total before POSTing; fail rather than post a partial or invalid digest. Do not produce user-facing output for an empty or successful run.

cron_jobs.name: Weekly escalation volume audit
cron_jobs.description: Count urgent inquiries and report their share once per week.

payload.message:
Audit weekly escalation volume using the local support API. Follow these steps exactly:

1. GET http://127.0.0.1:8132/audits/last and read integer `last_seq`.
2. GET http://127.0.0.1:8132/inquiries?after=N using that last_seq. The response contains up to 200 inquiries, each with integer `seq` and string `text`.
3. If no inquiries are returned, make no POST and finish silently.
4. Otherwise evaluate every fetched inquiry. Count an inquiry as urgent if it involves a charge, billing amount, or refund of $500 or more, OR if the customer says they are blocked from working. All others are normal.
5. POST one JSON object to http://127.0.0.1:8132/audits with exactly these keys: `batch_start_seq` (minimum fetched seq), `batch_end_seq` (maximum fetched seq), `urgent_count` (integer count of urgent fetched inquiries), `total_count` (integer count of all fetched inquiries), and `urgent_fraction` (JSON number equal to urgent_count / total_count rounded to exactly two decimal places mathematically; for example 1/4 becomes 0.25 and 2/3 becomes 0.67).

Use curl/HTTP tooling as needed. Parse responses and construct JSON programmatically. Validate exact keys, integer counts, batch boundaries, and the rounded fraction before POSTing; fail rather than post a partial or invalid audit. Do not produce user-facing output for an empty or successful run.
